text:
[Council File 26-1332]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE REPORT relative to the City’s compliance with Assembly Bill (AB) 1572 prohibiting the use of potable water to irrigate non-functional turf on most local government properties
Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. INSTRUCT the Bureau of Street Services (BSS), with the assistance of the Department of Water and Power (DWP), to report in 30 days on:
a. Existing conditions assessment and staffing needs necessary for BSS to assess its approximately 10 million square feet of improved landscaped medians, identify non-functional turf, document irrigation conditions and shared tree/landscape irrigation systems, and prioritize locations for conversion.
b. Conversion and maintenance resources necessary for BSS to establish and implement a phased Citywide median conversion program, including staffing and funding for design, construction, irrigation upgrades, plant establishment, and ongoing maintenance.
c. An initial list of potential medians for conversion, with at least one per Council District, that details all necessary capital expenses, to pilot a City Median Conversion Program.
d. A tailored City Median Conversion Program, developed in coordination with DWP, to facilitate AB 1572 compliance and implementation by BSS, including turf-conversion incentives, dedicated funding or financing mechanisms, and the process for receiving advanced lump sum payments and rebates for median conversion.
e. What will happen to existing non-compliant medians should they not be converted to drought- tolerant medians, including the potential increased annual maintenance costs due to weed removal, dust mitigation, and other issues as identified by BSS.
2. INSTRUCT the City Administrative Officer (CAO), in coordination with the Board of Public Works, BSS, and DWP, to report on potential front funding sources and grants, including but not limited to the Public Works Trust Fund, Measure M, state and federal grants, and other eligible sources.
3. REQUEST the DWP to confer with the Metropolitan Water District and report on the feasibility and process for increasing the rebate provided for turf conversion.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
Neither the CAO nor the Chief Legislative Analyst has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
Yes statement For:
Sylmar Neighborhood Council
(Energy and Environment Committee waived consideration of the above matter)
summary: Council asks whether the City complies with state law AB 1572, which bars using drinking water to irrigate non-functional turf on most government properties.

details.action: compliance review of state limits on potable water irrigation of non-functional turf
